claims.text: Conventional elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding undergo elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Excessive Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of the conventional coating.
The proposed intervention is a sub-micron Cr3Si interlayer between the zirconium-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating.
Depositing Cr3Si will produce a continuous nanoscale layer that acts as a physical and chemical barrier.
Cr3Si is thermodynamically stable at the relevant elevated temperatures.
Cr3Si has lower atomic diffusivity than elemental Cr and Zr.
Strong silicide bonding in Cr3Si reduces the mobility of Cr and Zr atoms.
The Cr3Si interlayer inhibits Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The outer Cr coating can form a corrosion-protective Cr2O3 passivation layer.
Adding the Cr3Si interlayer will still allow the outer Cr coating to form and retain a protective Cr2O3 scale.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the modified system will have a significantly thinner Cr–Zr interdiffusion zone.
The modified system will maintain intact oxide scales under both normal subcritical-water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam conditions.
Reduced interdiffusion and intact oxide scales will enhance coating integrity and prolong service life.
The proposed operating boundary extends from approximately 300 °C in subcritical water to approximately 1000 °C in high-temperature steam.
The high-temperature accident exposure boundary extends to several hours.

contradictions.description: The conditions field broadly describes exposure durations as being on the order of hours across the stated service range, whereas the boundary field distinguishes normal operational durations from only several hours of high-temperature steam exposure.
